text:
**My pick: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, about $700.** [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) ranks it best overall for CPAP. It has the quietest rating (about 20 dB under 200 W), a 10 ms UPS switchover, and a recharge in about 49 minutes. It runs about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.7 with it on. Those are calculated estimates, not lab tests. It isn't expandable. Price is from [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/), which has retailer buttons.

**Other good options**

- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, about $719.** It has the same capacity and UPS speed as the Anker, and it expands up to 5 kWh. That makes it the better choice if you also want whole-home outage backup. It's heavier at 27.6 lb. ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/))
- **Bluetti AC180, $499 ($474.05 with code AFF5OFF).** This is the best value for capacity. It has 1,152 Wh, about 3.1 nights humidifier-off and 1.4 on, and a 5-year warranty. Its UPS is slower at 20 ms, and it weighs about 16 kg (35 lb). [Buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link; the code was tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-21, but checkout has the final word). Details are on the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180).
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus, about $279–299.** It's light (10.4 lb) and cheap, but at 286 Wh it covers roughly one night with the humidifier off and not a full night with it on. Sources disagree here: [Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/) calls it multi-night, while [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) and [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) put it at under one night. I'd trust the math from those two.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, about $499.** It's the lightest 1 kWh unit and good for travel. However, Tested Watts notes Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices, and its UPS is up to 20 ms. I'd skip it for CPAP unless your CPAP maker okays it. ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/))

**Tips**

- **Humidifier:** It roughly doubles power draw. Turning it off during an outage stretches your charge the most.
- **DC cord:** Using your CPAP maker's 12V DC cord can add about 10–20% runtime ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)). Don't use a generic car adapter.
- **Sizing:** Aim for at least two nights. Capacity needed ≈ nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. With the humidifier on, that's about 1,200 Wh for two nights ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- **Your machine:** Check your CPAP's actual wattage, and ask your provider about a backup plan if you depend on therapy.

If you tell me whether you use the humidifier and whether you want this for travel or outages, I can narrow it to one.
